manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pour the trash from the cup into the red box; the cup does not need to be returned to its original place.

Task description: Pour the paper balls and other waste from the transparent cup into the red open box to the left of the cup in the image. Pick up the cup to pour; it does not need to be returned to its original position afterward.

Success criteria: The cup has been picked up, all waste has been poured into the red box, and no waste remains in the cup; the cup does not need to be returned to its original position.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping a wall section near the cup mouth away from the paper ball, with one finger inside and one outside. Obtain full pad contact below the rim and leave room for the trash to slide out.
- Match the gripper opening to the cup wall and the clearance needed for the fingertips to enter. Before closing, confirm the fingers are actually on opposite sides of the wall and grip moderately to reduce thin-wall deformation or slipping.
- Keep the cup opening up during transport. Test-lift slightly while off the table to check for slipping, avoiding an unstable grasp or spilling the trash prematurely.
- While pouring, keep the lower side of the cup opening above the inside of the red box opening, leaving room for the cup and gripper to rotate around the rim. Avoid dropping waste outside the box or hitting the rim with the cup body.
- If the paper ball does not slide out, slightly increase tilt or gently shake while maintaining a stable grasp and keeping the cup mouth directed into the box. Check the bottom and walls for remaining trash rather than judging completion merely because the cup was inverted.

I have read the manual and confirmed paper trash inside the clear cup and the red box to its left. The first lateral adjustment triggered a recoverable joint-limit rejection. The gripper is open and aligned with the cup wall on the left side of the opening. Next I will lower gradually, confirm one finger is inside and one outside the cup, then close and make a small test lift to check the grasp.

The projections of the two fingers are now on the inner and outer sides of the cup wall, and the cup remains on the table. I am lowering by no more than 1 cm per step while checking the actual contact point.
Both fingers have reached the cup wall below the rim. Next I will close the gripper and test-lift. I will judge whether the grasp is established by whether the cup rises steadily with the gripper.

The cup left its original position with the gripper during the test lift. After waiting, the grasp and cup orientation remained stable, with paper still inside. Next I will raise it and orient the wrist for clearance above the red box rim.
The cup remains suspended with opening around 4.9 mm and no paper wad seen falling out. I am raising it mouth upward, then will translate above the red box and pour in steps.
The cup is near the area above the red box rim, and the paper ball remains inside. I am switching to small lateral movements to confirm the cup opening is above the box before increasing the tilt.

The cup and paper ball remained stable during lateral movement, and the inside of the red box is now visible in the wrist camera. I need to move farther inward to leave room for the cup opening to move during pouring.

The cup remains securely grasped, and tipping has not started. I am continuing to adjust toward the inside of the red box; completion will be judged by whether the paper ball actually enters the box and whether anything remains in the cup.

The grasp point is above the box opening, but the cup opening is still toward the right side of the box. I will move inward a few more centimeters, then rotate a small angle around the gripper axis so the opening faces down into the box.

I began tilting slightly, and the grasp remains stable; the inside of the red box is visible below the cup opening. Next I will increase the tilt gradually and check each time whether the paper ball slides out.

The paper ball remains inside the cup as it tilts, and the red box opening is still below the cup rim. No drop is visible. I will increase the tilt slightly and stop to check for any remaining contents once the ball slides out.

The paper wad has moved toward the opening, but residue remains visible inside. Wrist rotation is near its limit. I will add one small angle and wait; if paper remains stuck, I will adjust the pouring pose based on observations.

After the small orientation adjustment, the paper wad slid out of the cup. The latest wrist image shows no residue on the bottom or walls, and the opening faces inside the red box. I will observe once more at rest, then end the episode for the on-site operator to confirm success.
